Device classification

The Zones, Lines and Departments catalogs used to classify appliances, where renaming a value moves every reference and removing one asks where its references go.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereGlobal ADOM → Administrator → Classification (URL /classification/)

What is it?#

Device Classification holds three catalogs:

  • Network Zones: where an appliance sits (for example dmz, internal).
  • Lines: the service line or environment (for example production, staging).
  • Departments: the owning team or function.

Each appliance is given one value per catalog on its Edit page. The same values group devices on the Architecture map and in the bookmarks rail. They also scope configuration baselines, network segments and line profiles.

Despite its place under this category, the page is not specific to FortiWeb. It is a console-wide administration page.

What does it do?#

The page edits one row per value, not a free-text list. That lets SATOM tell a rename from a delete:

  • Rename a value: every appliance, baseline combo, network segment and line profile that uses the old value is moved to the new one in the same save.
  • Remove a value that is in use: the save is refused until you choose, per value, under Move its references to:, whether its references are cleared (Clear them (leave unclassified)) or moved to another value of the same catalog.
  • In use by shows, per value, how many appliances (appl.), baseline combos (combo), network segments (seg.) and, for lines, line profiles (profile) reference it. These counts come from the live records, not from the catalog.
  • In use but not in this catalog lists values that records use but the catalog does not contain. Click one to add it as a new row, then save.

All three catalogs are validated before anything is written. Either the whole save succeeds or nothing changes.

Requirements#

  • None. The catalogs can be filled before any appliance exists.

Permissions#

users.manage is required to view and save (Administrator). The entry sits in the Administrator group, which is hidden without it, and /classification/ answers 403 Forbidden to other users.

The menu entry is in the Global ADOM. From the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator consoles the URL redirects to that console's home page.

How to use#

Add a value#

  1. Open Administrator → Classification in the Global ADOM.
  2. In the card of the catalog (Network Zones, Lines or Departments), click Add value and type the value.
  3. Click Save Classification.

Rename a value#

  1. Edit the text of the value in place.
  2. Click Save Classification. When references moved, the flash reads Classification saved. <n> reference(s) updated.

Remove a value#

  1. Click Remove on its row. The row is struck through, and a value that was never saved disappears at once.
  2. If the value is in use, choose under Move its references to: either Clear them (leave unclassified) or another value. The list offers the catalog's current values, including names you just typed.
  3. Click Save Classification.

Click Undo on a removed row to keep it after all.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Value The catalog entry. Unique per catalog, compared case-insensitively Yes dmz
Move its references to: For a removed value: — choose — (no decision), Clear them (leave unclassified), or another value Yes, when the value is in use internal

Example#

🧪Example — Normalising a zone name

Appliances were classified with the zone internal, and the team wants Internal. The admin edits the row to Internal and saves. SATOM moves the appliances, the baselines and the segments that held internal to Internal in one transaction. An automatically named baseline combo is renamed to match its new zone. If a combo for the new value already exists, the old combo is merged into it, and the flash adds <n> duplicate combo(s) absorbed.

Result#

  • The catalogs are saved, and references are moved, cleared or reassigned in the same transaction.
  • Clearing a line that has a line profile deletes that profile, because a profile without a line answers for nothing.
  • The Audit Log records classification.save with +added ~renamed -deleted per catalog and the number of references touched. A refused save is recorded as classification.refused.

Troubleshooting#

When a save is refused, the page comes back with your edits, not the stored catalog, so you can correct and resubmit. Every refusal message starts with the catalog name (zones:, lines: or departments:).

"'' is still used by appliance(s), baseline(s), segment(s) and line profile(s). Choose what happens to them before removing it."#

Possible causes - You removed a value that records still use, and left Move its references to: on — choose —. - For Lines, the value may be used only by a line profile; the message then counts it under line profile(s).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the refusal message and the In use by badges now count line profiles; before, a line used only by a line profile was refused with all counts at 0.

Solution 1. Pick Clear them (leave unclassified) or a replacement value. 2. Save again.

Verification - The flash reads Classification saved. <n> reference(s) updated.

"Cannot rename '' to '' in the same save that also changes ''. Do it in two steps."#

Possible causes - You swapped two values, or renamed a value onto a name that is itself being renamed or removed.

Solution 1. Rename one value to a temporary name and save. 2. Do the second rename and save again.

Verification - Each step saves without a refusal.

"'' is listed twice (also as ''). Values must be unique."#

Possible causes - Two rows hold the same value, possibly in different case.

Solution 1. Remove or rename one of them.

Verification - The save succeeds.

"'' is no longer in the catalog — it changed while this page was open. Reload and retry."#

Possible causes - Another admin saved the catalog after you opened the page.

Solution 1. Reload the page and repeat your edits.

Verification - The save succeeds.

"combo '' would merge into '', but it has template(s) that combo does not. Reassign or delete that combo first."#

Possible causes - The rename would make two baseline combos describe the same zone, line and department, and the one being absorbed has templates the other lacks.

Solution 1. Open the baseline combos under System provisioning profiles, and move or remove the extra templates. 2. Save the classification again.

Verification - The save succeeds and reports the combo as absorbed.

"line '' already has a profile in product '

', and '' has one too. …"#

Possible causes - Both lines have a line profile in the same product, so they cannot be merged.

Solution 1. Delete or edit one of the two line profiles. 2. Save the classification again.

Verification - The save succeeds.

Advanced#

Advanced How references are stored and moved
  • Zone, line and department are plain strings on appliances, on baselines and inside each network segment. There is no foreign key. That is why this page moves references explicitly.
  • Usage counts compare the exact stored string. dmz and DMZ are different values to the database, so they are counted separately.
  • A catalog value that the form did not send back is treated as a removal and goes through the same reference check.
  • A segment carries one zone and one line but a list of departments. Renaming a department rewrites it in that list.
